spots.name: Museo del Prado
spots.summary: The Museo del Prado, officially known as Museo Nacional del Prado, is the main Spanish national art museum, located in central Madrid.

spots.name: Almudena Cathedral
spots.summary: The Cathedral of Saint Mary the Royal of the Almudena, commonly known as the Almudena Cathedral, is a Catholic cathedral in Madrid, Spain. It is the seat of the Archdiocese of Madrid. Its construction began in 1883 and finished over a century later, when it was consecrated by Pope John Paul II in 1993.

spots.name: Royal Palace of Madrid
spots.summary: The Royal Palace of Madrid is the official residence of the Spanish royal family and is used primarily for state ceremonies.

spots.name: Main Square
spots.summary: The Plaza Mayor is the principal public square in the heart of Madrid, the capital of Spain. It was once the centre of Old Madrid. It was first built (1580–1619) during the reign of Philip III. Only a few blocks away is another famous plaza, the Puerta del Sol.

spots.name: Puerta del Sol
spots.summary: The Puerta del Sol is a public square in Madrid, one of the best known and busiest places in the city. This is the centre of the radial network of Spanish roads. The square also contains the famous clock whose bells mark the traditional eating of the Twelve Grapes and the beginning of a new year.

spots.name: Alcalá Gate
spots.summary: The Puerta de Alcalá is a Neo-classical gate in the Plaza de la Independencia in Madrid, Spain.

spots.name: Royal Spanish Academy

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Royal Spanish Academy is Spain's official royal institution with a mission to ensure the stability of the Spanish language. This is the official language regulating organ of Spain.

spots.name: Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía is Spain's national museum of 20th-century art. The museum was officially inaugurated on September 10, 1992, and is named for Queen Sofía. It is located in Madrid, near the Atocha train and metro stations, at the southern end of what is known as the Golden Triangle of Art.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía

spots.name: Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum
spots.summary: The Thyssen-Bornemisza National Museum, or simply the Thyssen, is an art museum in Madrid, Spain, located near the Prado Museum on one of the city's main boulevards. It is known as part of the "Golden Triangle of Art", which also includes the Prado and the Reina Sofía national galleries.

photo.author: Kyle Magnuson from Los Angeles, United States

spots.name: El Retiro Park
spots.summary: The Retiro Park, also known as Buen Retiro Park or simply El Retiro, is one of the largest city parks in Madrid, Spain. The park belonged to the Spanish monarchy until 1868, when it became a public park following the Glorious Revolution.

spots.name: Statue of the Bear and the Strawberry Tree
spots.summary: The Statue of the Bear and the Strawberry Tree is a sculpture from the second half of the 20th century, situated in the Spanish capital, Madrid.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Statue of the Bear and the Strawberry Tree

spots.name: Palacio de Cibeles

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cibeles Palace, formally known as Palacio de Comunicaciones and Palacio de Telecomunicaciones until 2011, is a complex composed of two buildings with white facades and is located in one of the historical centres of Madrid, Spain.

spots.name: Gran Vía
spots.summary: The Gran Vía is a street in central Madrid, Spain. It leads from Calle de Alcalá, close to Plaza de Cibeles, to Plaza de España. The street, sometimes referred to as the "Spanish Broadway", is one of the city's most important shopping areas, with a large number of hotels and large movie theatres.

spots.name: Plaza de Cibeles
spots.summary: The Plaza de Cibeles is a square with a neo-classical complex of marble sculptures with fountains that has become a symbol for the city of Madrid. It sits at the intersection of Calle de Alcalá, Paseo de Recoletos and Paseo del Prado.

photo.author: Miguel Diaz from Boadilla del Monte, España-Spain

spots.name: Temple of Debod

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Temple of Debod is an ancient Nubian temple currently located in Madrid, Spain. The temple was originally erected in the early 2nd century BC 15 km (9.3 mi) south of Aswan, Egypt.

spots.name: Las Ventas
spots.summary: The Plaza de Toros de Las Ventas, known simply as Las Ventas, is the largest bullfighting ring in Spain, located in the Guindalera quarter of the Salamanca district of Madrid. It was inaugurated on June 17, 1931.

spots.name: Torre Picasso

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Torre Picasso is a skyscraper in Madrid, Spain designed by Minoru Yamasaki. From 1988 until 2007 it was the tallest building in Madrid, measuring 515 ft (157 m) and with 43 floors. Torre Picasso is located next to the Pablo Picasso Square, within the commercial complex AZCA along the Paseo de la Castellana.

spots.name: Fountain of Cybele
spots.summary: The Fountain of Cybele is a neoclassical fountain in Madrid, Spain. It lies on the centre of the Plaza de Cibeles. The sculptural group in its centre represents Cybele, a Phrygian earth and fertility deity. It has become one of the icons of the city.

spots.name: Torre de Cristal

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torre de Cristal is a skyscraper in the Cuatro Torres Business Area (CTBA) in Madrid, Spain. Built between 2004 and 2008, the tower stands at 249 m (817 ft) tall with 52 floors and is the current tallest building in Spain, as well as the fifth-tallest in the European Union.

spots.name: National Museum of Archaeology

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The National Museum of Archaeology is a archaeology museum in Madrid, Spain. It is located on Calle de Serrano beside the Plaza de Colón, sharing its building with the National Library of Spain. It is one of the National Museums of Spain and it is attached to the Ministry of Culture.

spots.name: Biblioteca Nacional de España

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Biblioteca Nacional de España is the national library of Spain. It is the largest public library in the country, and one of the largest in the world. Founded in 1711, it is an autonomous agency attached to the Ministry of Culture since 1990.

spots.name: plaza de España
spots.summary: Plaza de España is a large square and popular tourist destination located in central Madrid, Spain at the western end of the Gran Vía. It features a monument to Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra and is adjacent to two of Madrid's most prominent skyscrapers.

spots.name: Torre Emperador

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torre Emperador Castellana, simply known as Torre Emperador and formerly named Torre Espacio, is an office skyscraper in Madrid, Spain, standing at 230 m (750 ft) tall and containing 57 floors. It is currently the fourth tallest building in Madrid.

spots.name: Cuatro Torres Business Area
spots.summary: The Cuatro Torres Business Area (CTBA), also known as the Área de Negocios de las Cuatro Torres, is a business district located in the Paseo de la Castellana in Madrid, Spain, on the former Ciudad Deportiva of Real Madrid.

spots.name: Torre Moeve

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torre Moeve is a skyscraper located in the Cuatro Torres Business Area in Madrid, Spain. With a height of 248.3 m (815 ft) and 45 floors, it is the second tallest building in Madrid and the second tallest in the Cuatro Torres Business Area after Torre de Cristal, which is taller by less than a metre.

spots.name: Edificio España
spots.summary: Hotel Riu Plaza España, commonly known by its historic name Edificio España, is a skyscraper and hotel in Madrid, Spain. It stands in Plaza de España, at the western end of Gran Vía. The building opened in 1953 as the Edificio España, a mixed-use complex containing a hotel, offices, apartments and shops.

spots.name: Paseo del Prado
spots.summary: The Paseo del Prado is one of the main boulevards in Madrid, Spain. It runs north–south between the Plaza de Cibeles and the Plaza del Emperador Carlos V, with the Plaza de Cánovas del Castillo lying approximately in the middle. The Paseo del Prado forms the southern end of the city's central axis.

spots.name: Gate of Europe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Gate of Europe towers, also known as KIO Towers/"Door of Europa", are twin office buildings near the Plaza de Castilla in Madrid, Spain. The towers have a height of 114 m (374 ft) and have 26 floors. They were constructed from 1989 to 1996.

spots.name: Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando, located on the Calle de Alcalá in the centre of Madrid, currently functions as a museum and gallery. A public law corporation, it is integrated together with other Spanish royal academies in the Instituto de España.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando

spots.name: Palace of Linares

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of Linares is a palace located in Madrid, Spain. It was declared national historic-artistic monument in 1976. Located at the plaza de Cibeles. It is the seat of the Casa de América.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Gryffindor assumed (based on copyright clai

spots.name: Torre de Madrid

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torre de Madrid is a high-rise mixed-use building in Madrid. It measures 142 metres in height, has 36 floors and was constructed between 1954 and 1957.

spots.name: Plaza de Colón
spots.summary: Plaza de Colón is located in the encounter of Chamberí, Centro and Salamanca districts of Madrid, Spain. This plaza and its fountain commemorate the explorer Christopher Columbus, whose name in Spanish was Cristóbal Colón, whose voyages to the Americas would lead to the creation of the Spanish Empire.

spots.name: Palacio de las Cortes

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of the Cortes, also known as the Palace of the Congress of Deputies, is the building that houses the Congress of Deputies, one of the two chambers of the Cortes Generales, the Spanish Parliament.

spots.name: Torres de Colón

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torres de Colón is a high-rise office building complex in the Plaza de Colón district of Madrid, Spain. Originally built between 1968 and 1976, and renovated in 2024, the complex consists of two twin towers standing at 115.1 m (378 ft) tall with 30 floors each. They were designed by Spanish architect Antonio Lamela.

spots.name: Torre PwC

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torre PwC, formerly known as Torre Sacyr Vallehermoso, is a mixed-use skyscraper located in Madrid, Spain. Built between 2004 and 2008, the tower stands at 236 m (774 ft) with 52 floors and is one of four buildings in the Cuatro Torres Business Area.

spots.name: Crystal Palace
spots.summary: The Palacio de Cristal is a 19th-century conservatory located in the Buen Retiro Park in Madrid, Spain. It is currently used for art exhibitions.

spots.name: Calle de Alcalá
spots.summary: Calle de Alcalá is among the longest streets in Madrid. It starts at the Puerta del Sol and goes on for 11 kilometres (6.8 mi), to the northeastern outskirts of the city. Henry David Inglis described it in 1837 as "long, of superb width, and flanked by a splendid range of unequal buildings".

spots.name: Arco de la Victoria
spots.summary: Arco de la Victoria is a triumphal arch built in the Moncloa district of Madrid, Spain. It is also known informally as the Puerta de Moncloa for its resemblance other Madrid landmarks, Puerta de Alcalá and Puerta de Toledo.

spots.name: Plaza de la Villa
spots.summary: The plaza de la Villa is an urban square in central Madrid, Spain. The square, bordering the Calle Mayor, houses some of the oldest buildings still around in the city.

spots.name: Plaza de Oriente
spots.summary: The Plaza de Oriente is a square in the historic center of Madrid, Spain. Rectangular in shape and monumental in character, it was designed in 1844 by Narciso Pascual y Colomer. The square was propagated by King Joseph I, who ordered the demolition of the medieval houses on the site.

spots.name: Paseo de la Castellana
spots.summary: Paseo de la Castellana, commonly known as La Castellana, is a major thoroughfare in Madrid, Spain. Cutting across the city from south to north, it has been described as the "true structuring axis" of the city.

spots.name: Church of Saint Jerome the Royal

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Jerome the Royal is a Roman Catholic church from the early 16th-century in central Madrid, Spain.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Saint Jerome the Royal

spots.name: Monument to Miguel de Cervantes
spots.summary: The Monument to Miguel de Cervantes is an instance of public art located in Madrid, Spain. Erected on the centre of the Plaza de España, it is dedicated to Miguel de Cervantes, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the Spanish language.

spots.name: Market of San Miguel
spots.summary: The Market of San Miguel is a covered market located in Madrid, Spain. Originally built in 1916, it was purchased by private investors in 2003 who renovated the iron structure and reopened it in 2009.

photo.author: Juan Antonio Flores Segal from Madrid (Spain)

spots.name: Torres Blancas

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Torres Blancas is a mixed use concrete building in Madrid, Spain, designed in 1961 by Spanish architect Francisco Javier Sáenz de Oiza. The structure is a noted example of Spanish Organicism. Spanish industrialist Juan Huarte commissioned the project which initially included two residential towers.

spots.name: Callao Square
spots.summary: The Callao Square is located at the centre of the Spanish capital of Madrid.

photo.author: Alfredo Sánchez Romero from Madrid, España

spots.name: Fountain of Neptune
spots.summary: The Fountain of Neptune is a neoclassical fountain located in Madrid, Spain. It lies on the centre of the Plaza de Cánovas del Castillo, a roundabout in the Paseo del Prado. The sculptural group in its centre represents Neptune, a Roman water deity.

photo.author: Dirección General de Turismo. Consejería de Economía e Innovación Tecnológica. C

spots.name: Royal Basilica of Saint Francis the Great
spots.summary: The Royal Basilica of Saint Francis the Great is a Roman Catholic basilica in central Madrid, Spain, located in the neighborhood of Palacio.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Royal Basilica of Saint Francis the Great

spots.name: Santa Cruz Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palacio de Santa Cruz or Palace of the Holy Cross is a baroque building in central Madrid, Spain. It now houses the Spanish Foreign Ministry. It was used as a jail until the reign of Philip IV of Spain, when it was converted into a palace.

spots.name: Fuente del Ángel Caído
spots.summary: The Fuente del Ángel Caído is a fountain located in the Buen Retiro Park in Madrid, Spain. Its sculptors were Ricardo Bellver and Francisco Jareño y Alarcón (pedestal).

spots.name: Real Jardín Botánico de Madrid
spots.summary: Real Jardín Botánico de Madrid is an 8 hectares botanical garden in Madrid (Spain). The public entrance is located at Plaza de Murillo, next to the Prado Museum.

spots.name: Torrespaña

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Torrespaña is a 232 m (761.15 ft) high reinforced concrete freestanding broadcasting tower in Madrid, Spain. It is the central and main transmission node of the terrestrial television and radio networks in the country as well as the station that covers the city and its metropolitan area.

spots.name: Buen Retiro Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Buen Retiro Palace in Madrid was a large palace complex designed by the architect Alonso Carbonell and built on the orders of Philip IV of Spain as a secondary residence and place of recreation. It was built in what was then the eastern limits of the city of Madrid.

spots.name: Residencia de Estudiantes
spots.summary: The Residencia de Estudiantes, literally the "Student Residence", is a centre of Spanish cultural life in Madrid. The Residence was founded to provide accommodation for students along the lines of classic colleges at Bologna, Salamanca, Cambridge, or Oxford.

spots.name: Royal Collections Gallery
spots.summary: The Royal Collections Gallery, originally named the Royal Collections Museum, is an art museum in Madrid. Run by Patrimonio Nacional, it is located in a new building above the gardens of the Campo del Moro park and next to the Almudena Cathedral and the Royal Palace.

spots.name: Basílica pontificia de San Miguel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Pontifical Basilica of Saint Michael is a Baroque-style Catholic church and minor basilica in central Madrid, Spain. It is located in San Justo Street, adjacent to the Archbishop's Palace.

spots.name: Cerralbo Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Cerralbo Museum is an art museum in Madrid, Spain. It houses the art and historical object collections of Enrique de Aguilera y Gamboa, Marquis of Cerralbo, who died in 1922. It is one of the National Museums of Spain and it is attached to the Ministry of Culture.

spots.name: Church of San José

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of San José is a church located on the Calle de Alcalá in Madrid, Spain. The church in the past belonged to the former convent of San Hermenegildo, established in 1586 by Friar Nicolás de Jesús y María. The church was declared Bien de Interés Cultural in 1995.

spots.name: Palacio Vistalegre
spots.summary: The Palacio Vistalegre is a multipurpose arena located in Madrid, Spain. It was built on the site of the former bullring, "Plaza de toros de Vista Alegre", inaugurated in 1908 and demolished in 1995. The venue is composed of three main spaces: The Arena, The Centre and the Sala San Miguel.

spots.name: Monument to Philip IV of Spain
spots.summary: The Monument to Philip IV or Fountain of Philip IV is a memorial to Philip IV of Spain in the centre of Plaza de Oriente in Madrid, Spain.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monument to Philip IV of Spain

spots.name: Estación de Chamberí

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sun

spots.summary: Former metro station designed by architect Antonio Palacios (creator of the Palacio de Cibeles, Círculo de Bellas Artes and Hospital de Maudes). It was inaugurated in 1919, but closed in 1966, thereby becoming a "ghost station". Since 2008 it has been converted to a museum, exhibiting original counters, signs, maps and advertising posters from earlier ages.

spots.name: Faro de Moncloa
spots.summary: A {{m

spots.name: Rosaleda del Parque del Oeste
spots.summary: The rose garden of Madrid, located in the same park as the Templo de Debod. If you like roses and are in Madrid when they have flowered, definitely worth a visit. The garden holds an international competition yearly.

photo.author: manuel m. v. from Valdemoro, Spain

spots.name: La Tabacalera
spots.summary: An abandoned tobacco factory turned into a huge Berlin-like alternative art space driven by the diverse locals of Lavapies district. Also free workshops daily. Nice big cheap outdoors terrace.It is hoped that the closure is temporary and that it will return in a reduced form after works, check website for current situation.

spots.name: Planetario de Madrid

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Features several exhibits related to space exploration, two screens playing documentaries, an interactive area and, of course, the planetarium. Projections last 45 minutes each. Different ones play on different days, so check their website. All the exhibits are explained in Spanish only and the projections in the planetarium are also in Spanish.

spots.name: Mercado de la Cebada

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Once a glass and iron market of the late 19th century, it is now a vaulted concrete building which still serves as a neighborhood market. Where it used to stand an annexed public swimming pool and sports facilities, it lies now an empty field, used and managed by a neighbor association.
